data.body:
PHASE 1 ROOT CAUSE — CONFIRMED BY RUNTIME OBSERVATION (rebar-debug). No live Jira was touched.

## Mechanism (confirmed)

`pytest-xdist` reads the `xdist_group` mark in exactly ONE scheduler. Installed xdist 3.8.0:
`xdist/scheduler/loadgroup.py:11-47` is the only scheduler that computes a group scope;
`scheduler/load.py` and `scheduler/worksteal.py` contain **zero** occurrences of `group`
(`grep -c group` returns 0 for both). Under any other `--dist` mode the mark is parsed
(`xdist/remote.py:245`) and then discarded — no error, no warning. Silently inert.

## Discriminating experiment (RUNTIME, not source-reading)

8 tests marked `xdist_group("live_reconcile_e2e")` + 8 unmarked tests, `-n 4`, each test
recording `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` to a file. Same tests, three dist modes, this worktree's venv
(xdist 3.8.0). Observed worker placement of the 8 GROUPED tests:

    --dist load        -> gw0 gw0 gw1 gw1 gw2 gw2 gw3 gw3   (scattered over 4 workers)
    --dist worksteal   -> gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0 gw1 gw1 gw1 gw1   (scattered over 2 workers)
    --dist loadgroup   -> gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0   (confined to 1 worker)

The `loadgroup` arm is the negative control: it proves xdist, the mark, and the harness are all
working, so the scattering under `load`/`worksteal` is the scheduler ignoring the group and not a
broken probe. This discriminates "the mark is inert outside loadgroup" from "the mark never
works" and from "xdist is misconfigured here".

The same run also proves the (b) half: under `--dist loadgroup`, the UNGROUPED tests landed on
gw1/gw2/gw3 **while** the grouped set occupied gw0 — i.e. an ungrouped live-Jira test runs
CONCURRENTLY with the confined group even in the CI lane that does pass `--dist loadgroup`.

## Where the invariant actually breaks

Two independent breaks, one shared cause:

(a) NO configured local invocation honours the group. `pyproject.toml:599` sets only
    `addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config"` — no `-n`, no `--dist`; there is no
    `pytest.ini`/`setup.cfg`/`tox.ini`. So an ad-hoc `pytest -n auto` gets xdist's default
    `--dist load`, and the documented local command (`docs/coverage.md:47`) is
    `--dist worksteal`. Both ignore the group. Note this is BROADER than the ticket's framing:
    worksteal, not just load, drops it — and worksteal is what the project documents.

(b) A live-Jira test carries no group at all.
    `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py:155` `test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira` is
    `@pytest.mark.integration` and issues a real project-wide inbound JQL fetch whenever `acli`
    is on PATH and `JIRA_PROJECT` is set. It has no `xdist_group`. Because it IS in the
    integration tier, it runs in CI's `--dist loadgroup` lane — and, per the experiment above,
    lands on a different worker from the E2E group. So this break is live in CI's own lane, not
    only locally.

Corroborating the ticket's note: `test_delete_permission_probe`
(`tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py:334`) is the ONLY `@_requires_live` test in its
module — every other test there is offline/deterministic. So the intra-module group buys nothing
by itself; the counterparty it needs to be serialised against is precisely the ungrouped test in
(b).

## Legitimacy: `defect` (not intended behaviour, not a feature request)

Cited authority — story 8d36 `curricular-brickred-ratfish` (8d36-a15a-fcbd-4ebd, CLOSED), which
introduced xdist parallelism, states the invariant in its own description:

  "Integration tier: parallelize only NON-live tests. ... Live tests ([integration, live], e.g.
   test_reconcile_live_e2e.py) share one live Jira project and flake under parallel load
   (eventual-consistency); keep them serial or confine to one worker via
   @pytest.mark.xdist_group + --dist loadgroup. In CI's integration job they self-skip without
   Jira creds, BUT THE COMMAND MUST NOT ASSUME THAT."

and its commit body (f943c7ef58): "test_reconcile_live_e2e.py: xdist_group so the live-Jira
reconciler E2E stays serial". The shipped code takes the confinement arm, so the invariant it
must hold is "every live-Jira-touching test is group-confined, wherever it can run". Both (a) and
(b) violate it. The final clause of 8d36 forecloses the obvious defence ("they skip in CI").

I checked the not-a-bug case before concluding. The strongest one available is that the E2E
module docstring (lines 59-63) DOES name loadgroup — "even when the integration tier is
parallelized with `-n>0 --dist loadgroup`" — so it is not simply lying, which is a real point
against AC1's "correct the docstring" arm as stated. But the same comment then closes with "so
this only matters on a local live run", and a local live run is exactly the context where no
loadgroup is configured. The comment promises the protection precisely where it is absent. That
is a defect against 8d36's invariant, not a doc nit.

## Harm today: LATENT, not active — and that shapes the fix

Being straight about this, because it drives urgency:
- In CI, both live tests self-skip (no `acli`, no creds). No traffic, so no collision today.
- `make test` is `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q` — serial, and it deselects
  the live tests anyway. The documented local coverage command deselects them too.
- So no CURRENTLY-CONFIGURED invocation actually runs two live-Jira tests concurrently.
- But the exposure is real and this project has stood in it: d30c's regression comment records a
  "complete local xdist inventory with live Jira credentials present" on 2026-08-18 — an ad-hoc
  full-suite xdist run with creds is a thing that happens here. In that run the two live tests
  share one Jira Cloud account's rate budget and one project's search index, and the E2E probe's
  whole assertion is about index convergence timing.

I did NOT attempt a live-Jira reproduction: the bridge is paused for a duplicate-comment cleanup
and any write would interfere. The harm claim is therefore reasoned exposure, not an observed
collision, and I am labelling it as such rather than overstating it.

Consequence for the fix: the right move is to restore the invariant cheaply and make its absence
LOUD — not to re-architect scheduling. Specifically, I am NOT putting `--dist loadgroup` into
`pyproject.toml` addopts, as AC1 suggests as one option. Three reasons: (1) it re-schedules all
~14k tests in every local `-n` run, discarding worksteal's dynamic rebalancing that 8d36 chose
deliberately and docs/coverage.md documents; (2) addopts are PREPENDED, so CI's explicit
`--dist worksteal` still wins — the setting would look like protection while doing nothing in the
lane it appears to cover; (3) it does not fix (b) at all.

## Defect origin (caused_by)

**8d36-a15a-fcbd-4ebd** (`curricular-brickred-ratfish`), commit **f943c7ef58** (2026-07-13),
trailer `rebar-ticket: 8d36-a15a-fcbd-4ebd`. That commit introduced `-n` + `--dist` and added the
`xdist_group` mark — i.e. it CREATED the obligation and shipped without meeting it for the second
live-Jira test. Before it, nothing ran in parallel, so live-Jira traffic was serialised by
construction; after it, it is not. Classified `regression` on that basis.

Divergence from what a mechanical blame would say, recorded per protocol: this is an UNMET
OBLIGATION, so the fix site is not the cause site. `git blame` on
`tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` names 7a7a439309 (2026-06-15, "split tests/interfaces into
seam subdirectories") — a file-move carrier, and one that PREDATES the transition, which is the
date test failing. That test's lines were correct when written; they became wrong when 8d36 added
parallelism around them. Attributing to the consumer's old commit would charge the defect to the
wrong work item. `88cc31390c` (2b60) is likewise a carrier — it only relocated the `--dist
loadgroup` line into a reusable workflow. Searches run: `git log -S'--dist loadgroup'`,
`git log -S'xdist_group("live_reconcile_e2e")'`, `git log -S'test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira'`.
